name: Ibneiah
overview: Ibneiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified in Scripture as the son of Jeroham. His mention is brief, with no additional notes or detailed narrative provided. His lineage places him within the post-exilic community recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8.
namesAndTitles: The name Ibneiah means "y-h-v-h built," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's role in his identity or heritage. This name is a proper name found specifically in 1 Chronicles 9:8 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Ibneiah is explicitly identified as the son of Jeroham, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Ibneiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical mention, which serves to document the restoration of the community of Benjamin after the exile. His inclusion in the genealogical record underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving His people and maintaining their tribal identities, which is foundational for understanding the continuity of God's covenant people.
